recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not add experimental elements to current core ValueSet sources solely for FHIR-34450. If a future build emits a ValueSet that asserts ShareableValueSet without experimental, address the canonical-resource tooling or current CRMI/profile-maintenance source rather than reintroducing obsolete core ShareableValueSet assumptions.
issue_request: FHIR-34450 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction against R4B ValueSet examples that asserted http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/shareablevalueset while missing required ValueSet.experimental; the resolution requested tooling to set experimental=true for examples and false for non-examples unless already declared.
initial_application: Jira records the fix as pre-applied in R4B and R5, with additional fixes in HL7/kindling#69. The merged Kindling change explicitly cites FHIR-34450 and adds canonical-resource processing that sets experimental from example status, warns on disagreement, and calls the fix for ValueSet examples before serialization.
additional_context: FHIR-37449 is the direct follow-up from the same reporter and is already represented on the combined branch. Later profile-family decisions changed the current core interpretation: FHIR-29943 and FHIR-31395 revised the R5 ValueSet profile family, FHIR-38672/FHIR-39143 retained experimental where ShareableValueSet was imposed, and FHIR-37959 later moved the Shareable/Publishable/Computable/Executable profile family out of core for CRMI maintenance. Current fhir.ini and ValueSet-core inputs no longer define an active core ShareableValueSet profile.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. A current source scan found 21 XML ValueSets without explicit experimental, but zero XML ValueSets asserting ShareableValueSet, so the invalid condition reported by FHIR-34450 is absent. Spot checks of build.fhir.org for ValueSets whose source omits experimental show generated experimental=false, matching the accepted tooling rule.
